chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ismail ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the servant's sins are numerous and he does not have with him from his deeds that would expiate them, He tests him with grief to expiate them.'
ai.seo_question: How does grief expiate sins in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the concept of 'hastening punishment' (ta'jil al-'adhab), where grief serves as a gentle, worldly expiation for sins when good deeds are insufficient. This highlights the Shia understanding of divine mercy, where emotional trials act as a purifying mechanism to cleanse the soul before the Hereafter. The emphasis on 'al-huzn' (grief/sorrow) underscores the spiritual value of introspective suffering as a form of worship and purification.
